- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.22 or lower) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast slope in next 5-7 days to align with historical mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.17) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates continuation — increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (0.17+), model frequently overestimates upside — cap forecast growth at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overbought bias.  
- If true outcome deviates >3% from 30d forecast in first 5 days, model is likely lagging — adjust forecast early by +1–2% to catch momentum.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., -2%+ over 10+ days), model is overestimating — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
